traps.label: "** DADDY POP Included" inside every Featured party description (ENERGY, DRENCH, GRIP, SLICK, GROOVE, SNOUT, STEER, TOOLSHED)
traps.why: The Featured parties' text mentions the same-night Bear Cave DADDY POP as part of the ticket. DADDY POP already has its own row for that date (Friday and Saturday series); the phrase must not spawn a second DADDY POP record or be merged into the Featured party's title.

traps.label: "Happy Hour 5 PM – 9 PM – CODE BAR Bear Cave Opens 8 PM" / "Happy Hour 7 PM – 9 PM CODE Bar Opens 7 PM | Tavern Opens 9 PM" at the top of most descriptions
traps.why: The bar's opening hours are pasted ahead of the event's own line in the description of nearly every row. They are venue hours, not an event: a "Happy Hour" record or a start time of 5 PM for a 9 PM party would be wrong (the feed's own start_date already leans to the happy-hour time on the weekday series — recorded as published, noted per event).

evidence.quote: Happy Hour 5 PM – 9 PM – CODE BAR Bear Cave Opens 8 PM

traps.label: "HAPPY HOUR ALL NIGHT For Anyone Wearing Jock Strap + No Pants*" (Mon), "… Singlets or Underwear …" (Wed), "… A Harness or Fetish Gear*" (Thu)
traps.why: The Tuesday event is TITLED "HAPPY HOUR ALL NIGHT"; the same phrase inside the Monday/Wednesday/Thursday descriptions is a drink deal for people in gear, not a second event on those nights. Title matching on the phrase would fold three series into the Tuesday one.

evidence.quote: HAPPY HOUR ALL NIGHT For Anyone Wearing Jock Strap + No Pants*

traps.label: "SOUTH FLORIDA FOOT MEN BAR NIGHT 5 PM – 7 PM Second Saturday of Every Month" on a row dated the THIRD Saturday (Sep 19) with a poster named …_QUARTERLY
traps.why: The description asserts a monthly second-Saturday rule that the site's own dates contradict (only Sep 19 is listed, in any of the 550 rows). The Sep 19 record is real and expected; a monthly recurrence derived from the blurb is not.

evidence.quote: SOUTH FLORIDA FOOT MEN BAR NIGHT 5 PM – 7 PM Second Saturday of Every Month

traps.label: ENERGY and DADDY POP on 2026-09-11 — the first two REST rows, over by recon
traps.why: REST's server-set start_date is 2026-09-11 04:00:00, so on Sep 12 the feed still returns Friday night; the ICS export and the /calendar2/ list both start at Sep 12. Extracting them is correct under allowPastEvents; they must keep the Sep 11 date.

traps.label: — the Divi month grid on the configured page is empty in static HTML
traps.why: The grid is filled client-side; a static read of /calendar2/ sees only the 10-row list module below it and a "Load More" button. Not an event, and not evidence that the site has 10 events — the REST door is the complete listing.

traps.label: 550 REST rows: the five permanent series pre-expanded weekly through 2028-09-11 (e.g. JOCK STRAP NIGHT ×105 occurrences)
traps.why: Each far-future row is a real occurrence the site lists, but 550 rows are 23 events. A run that writes one record per row (the 2026-09-12 trial wrote 346 from pages 1–7) is materializing two years of a weekly series; this file materializes only the window. Beyond-window rows are not wrong extractions, they are outside what this file asserts.

expect.note: How far ahead series occurrences should be materialized is the scraper's policy, not the site's; the site's answer is two years.

openQuestions.q: DADDY POP Fridays (slug daddy-pop-5-3-3) stop after 2027-04-30 while DADDY POP Saturdays run to the end of the feed — is the Friday edition ending, or was the series simply created with a shorter horizon? Only the site owner knows; the file records what is listed.

Weekday series start_date is the happy-hour time (19:00 / 17:00) while the description gives the event's own time (9 PM / 8 PM). Which should the calendar show as startTime? Recorded as published (feed start_date) with the description time in each note.
REST pages 9–10 were closed by arithmetic (exactly 100 slots for 100 rows); a future recon with request budget should read them once to confirm.
